root_cause.text: Missing validation in the openvswitch `validate_set()` function that the MPLS action payload length matches the fixed size of `struct ovs_key_mpls`, allowing variable-sized data to be passed to action handling which expects a fixed-size structure, potentially leading to memory corruption or out-of-bounds access.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states "validate_set() accepted OVS_KEY_ATTR_MPLS as variable-sized payload for SET/SET_MASKED actions. In action handling, OVS expects fixed-size MPLS key data (struct ovs_key_mpls)." The patch adds the check `if (key_len != sizeof(struct ovs_key_mpls)) return -EINVAL;` to reject non-matching payload lengths.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add length validation for MPLS key attribute in OVS set validation to prevent invalid attribute sizes.
intent_record.what: Added a check in the OVS_KEY_ATTR_MPLS case of validate_set to verify that key_len equals sizeof(struct ovs_key_mpls); if not, return -EINVAL.
intent_record.how: The change ensures that the length of the MPLS key attribute matches the expected structure size, preventing potential out-of-bounds access or incorrect parsing from malformed attributes.

candidates.rationale: This case entry does not validate that the attribute length matches the expected fixed size of struct ovs_key_mpls, allowing variable-sized data to be passed and leading to potential memory corruption.
This break allows the switch to exit without performing any length validation on the MPLS attribute, permitting undersized data to be used by subsequent action handling.
This condition only checks the ethertype but not the attribute length, so it is insufficient to guard against size mismatches that could cause out-of-bounds access.
